ai.description: This stout snake reaches 60–90 cm. It is yellowish-brown with dark brown dorsal blotches and a white belly. Key features include a blunt, wedge-shaped head and a short, heavily keeled, conical tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Rough-tailed Sand Boa (*Eryx conicus*) is best distinguished by its strongly keeled, rough scales that give it a sandpaper-like texture, unlike the smooth scales of other Indian sand boas.
ai.habitat: *Eryx conicus* inhabits arid to semi-arid regions, including sandy plains, scrub forests, and rocky foothills, typically at elevations from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Rough-tailed Sand Boa is primarily nocturnal and utilizes a "sit-and-wait" ambush strategy, burying itself in loose soil to surprise passing prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eryx conicus* is ovoviviparous, typically breeding from January to April. Females produce litters of 6–14 young, usually born between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eryx conicus* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the arid plains of Pakistan and India to elevations of 1,500 meters in the Himalayas.
